questions.text_english:
(1) Plastic pollution has become one of the most pressing environmental issues, as rapidly increasing production of disposable plastic products overwhelms the world's ability to deal with them. Plastic pollution is most visible in developing Asian and African nations, where garbage collection systems are often inefficient or nonexistent. But the developed world, especially in countries with low recycling rates, also has trouble properly collecting discarded plastics. Plastic trash has become so ubiquitous that it has prompted efforts to write a global treaty negotiated by the United Nations.

(2) Plastics made from fossil fuels are just over a century old. Production and development of thousands of new plastic products accelerated after World War II. It transformed the modern age so much that life without plastics is unrecognizable today. Plastics revolutionized medicine with life-saving devices, made space travel possible, lightened cars and jets - saving fuel and pollution - and saved lives with helmets, incubators, and equipment for clean drinking water.

(3) The conveniences plastics offer, however, led to a throw-away culture that reveals the material's dark side today, single-use plastics account for 40 percent of the plastic produced every year. Many of these products, such as plastic bags and food wrappers, have a lifespan of mere minutes to hours, yet they may persist in the environment for hundreds of years.

(4) Most of the plastic trash in the oceans, Earth's last sink, flows from land. Trash is also carried to sea by major rivers, which act as conveyor belts, picking up more and more trash as they move downstream. Once at sea, much of the plastic trash remains in coastal waters. But once caught up in ocean currents, it can be transported around the world.

(5) Millions of animals are killed by plastics every year, from birds to fish to other marine organisms. Nearly 700 species, including endangered ones, are known to have been affected by plastics. Nearly every species of seabirds eats plastics. Most of the deaths of animals are caused by entanglement or starvation. Seals, whales, turtles, and other animals are strangled by abandoned fishing gear or discarded six-pack rings.

(6) The solution is to prevent plastic waste from entering rivers and seas in the first place, many scientists and conservationists including the National Geographic Society say. This could be accomplished with improved waste management systems and recycling, better product design that takes into account the short life of disposable packaging, and reduction in manufacturing of unnecessary single-use plastics.
questions.instruction_line_english: Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions based on it:

sub_questions.text_english: Which of the following statements best describes the reason why plastic pollution has become one of the most pressing environmental issues?

options_english.A: Plastic trash collection systems have become inefficient or nonexistent.
options_english.B: Rapidly increasing production of disposable plastic products overwhelms the world's ability to deal with them.
options_english.C: Some plastics have a lifespan of mere minutes to hours, yet they may persist in the environment for hundreds of years.
options_english.D: The developed world, especially in countries with low recycling rates, has trouble properly collecting plastics.

sub_questions.solution: Option B is correct. The passage explicitly states in the very first paragraph that plastic pollution is pressing because 'rapidly increasing production of disposable plastic products overwhelms the world's ability to deal with them.'

sub_questions.text_english: What is the tone of the writer in the given lines from paragraph 2? Rationalise your response in about 40 words. 'It transformed the modern age so much that life without plastics is unrecognizable today.'

key_points: Objective and factual tone.
Acknowledges the immense utility and revolutionary impact of plastic on modern life.

sub_questions.solution: The tone of the writer is objective and deeply appreciative. The writer states historical facts regarding how plastic completely transformed modern life, acknowledging its immense, revolutionary utility before moving on to discuss the devastating throw-away culture it birthed.

sub_questions.text_english:
The passage includes some words that are opposites of each other. From the sets (A) - (E) below, identify two sets of synonyms.
(A) garbage and trash
(B) starvation and strangled
(C) disposable and reduction
(D) persist and downstream
(E) transformed and revolutionized

key_points: (A) garbage and trash
(E) transformed and revolutionized

sub_questions.solution: The two correct sets of synonyms from the given options are set (A) 'garbage and trash' and set (E) 'transformed and revolutionized', as both pairs contain words with similar meanings in the context of the given passage.

sub_questions.text_english: Complete the sentence appropriately : The writer says that most of the plastic trash is found in the Earth's last sink and the reason it is transported around the world is _______
sub_questions.solution: According to paragraph 4, the reason plastic trash is transported completely around the world is that it gets caught up in ocean currents.

sub_questions.text_english: Based on the reading of the passage, examine, in about 40 words, the downside of the convenience that plastic offers.

key_points: Creation of a harmful throw-away culture.
Single-use plastics have a very short lifespan but persist in the environment for centuries.

sub_questions.solution: The immense convenience of plastics has birthed a highly destructive throw-away culture. Single-use plastics, despite having a lifespan of mere minutes or hours, persist in the natural environment for hundreds of years, polluting oceans and severely overwhelming global waste systems.

sub_questions.text_english: Complete the sentence appropriately : According to conservationists, the two ways in which most of the deaths of animals are caused are _______
sub_questions.solution: Paragraph 5 explicitly states that most of the deaths of animals caused by plastic pollution are due to entanglement or starvation.

sub_questions.text_english: Based on the passage, how can we contribute to the reduction of plastic waste?

options_english.A: by internationalising the waste management system
options_english.B: by minimizing the use of single-use plastics
options_english.D: by not using helmets made of plastic

sub_questions.solution: Option B is correct. The final paragraph specifically points to the 'reduction in manufacturing of unnecessary single-use plastics' as a primary solution to prevent plastic waste from polluting the environment.

sub_questions.text_english: State one reason why plastic pollution is most visible in developing Asian and African nations.

key_points: Garbage collection systems are often inefficient or nonexistent.

sub_questions.solution: Plastic pollution is most visible in developing Asian and African nations primarily because their garbage collection and waste management systems are often highly inefficient or completely nonexistent.

questions.text_english:
(1) Rotation of crops is a universal phenomenon which is practised by most of the farmers of the tropical and temperate countries. The main objective of rotation of crops is to obtain higher agricultural returns on the one hand, and to maintain the soil fertility on the other.

(2) In other words, the rotation of crops helps in making agriculture more sustainable. The importance of crop rotation is more in the areas where farmers grow two, or more than two crops in the same field in a year. Irrigation facilities have also been appreciably developed in the country during the last three decades. The availability of water to the arable land has helped in the intensification of agriculture.

(3) In the areas such as Punjab and Haryana, where the Green Revolution is a big success, one soil exhaustive crop (rice) is followed by another soil exhaustive crop (wheat). Subsequently, the field vacated by wheat is devoted to either rice or maize or cotton. Thus, in one year, the farmers are harvesting three soil exhaustive crops from the same field. Such a rotation of crops may fetch more income to the farmers, but depletes the soil fertility at a faster pace.

(4) A number of field studies were conducted to assess the traditional crop rotation pattern. One such field study about the changes in the rotation of crops was conducted in the village Banhera (Tanda), Haridwar district. The main rotation of crops of the village is shown in the table below.

Traditional Rotation of Crops (1960-65) in Banhera (Tanda)
Year | Kharif (mid-June to mid-October) | Rabi (mid-October to mid-April) | Zaid (April to June) | No. of days land left fallow
1960 | Millet/fodder/rice | Gram | Fallow | 90
1961 | Fallow | Wheat | Fallow | 210
1962 | Millet/fodder/rice | Gram | Fallow | 90
1963 | Fallow | Wheat | Fallow | 210
1964 | Millet mixed with urad/fodder/rice | Gram | Fallow | 90
1965 | Fallow | Wheat | Fallow | 210
questions.instruction_line_english: Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions based on it:

sub_questions.text_english: Fill in the blanks with the appropriate option from those given in brackets, based on your understanding of para 2. One of the reasons that there has been an intensification of agriculture in the country is the development of irrigation facilities is a/an _______ (fact/opinion) because it is a/an _______ (subjective judgement/objective detail).
sub_questions.solution: The development of irrigation facilities leading to intensification is a 'fact' because it is an 'objective detail' that has been visibly and statistically developed in the country over the last three decades, not a personal belief.

sub_questions.text_english: Based on your understanding of paras 1 and 2, state whether the following statement is true or false. If proper irrigation facility is provided, higher agricultural returns can be obtained by making crop rotation more sustainable.
sub_questions.solution: The statement is inherently false in the context of the entire passage. While proper irrigation aids intensification, paragraph 3 warns that intensely obtaining higher returns through consecutive exhaustive crops actively depletes soil fertility, making it less sustainable, not more.

sub_questions.text_english: Justify the following in about 40 words. Crop rotation may fetch more income to the farmers, but depletes the soil fertility at a faster pace.

key_points: Growing consecutive soil exhaustive crops yields more harvests per year.
This intense continuous extraction rapidly exhausts the soil's natural nutrients.

sub_questions.solution: Growing multiple soil-exhaustive crops consecutively, such as planting rice followed immediately by wheat, allows farmers to harvest up to three crops a year, thereby drastically increasing their immediate income. However, this aggressive, continuous nutrient extraction rapidly exhausts and depletes the soil's natural fertility.

sub_questions.text_english: Based on the table, mention the years when the land was left fallow for maximum number of days.
sub_questions.solution: According to the provided table, the land was left completely fallow for the maximum number of days, which is 210 days, in the specific years 1961, 1963, and 1965.

sub_questions.text_english: The study conducted in village Banhera (Tanda) reflects that during the years 1960 to 1965, from April to June, the land was left fallow or uncultivated throughout. State any one inference that can be drawn from this.

key_points: Lack of irrigation facilities during the dry summer season.

sub_questions.solution: A logical inference is that there was a severe lack of adequate irrigation facilities during the hot, dry Zaid season (April to June), making agricultural cultivation entirely impossible during those months.

sub_questions.text_english:
Select the option that correctly states the significance of crop rotation as given below :
(1) Crop rotation is done to obtain higher agricultural returns.
(2) Higher agricultural returns can be obtained by harvesting soil exhaustive crops.
(3) Crop rotation demands that land should be left fallow for a few months to increase the fertility of soil.
(4) Better irrigation facility to the arable land has helped in the intensification of agriculture.
(5) If crops to be harvested are chosen wisely, crop rotation can help in maintaining fertility of soil.
sub_questions.solution: Option D is correct. Paragraph 1 clearly states that the core objectives and significance of crop rotation are to obtain higher agricultural returns (1) and to maintain the soil fertility (5) if managed and chosen wisely.

sub_questions.text_english: Crop rotation is helping in making agriculture more sustainable. Mention one benefit and one drawback of crop rotation. (Answer in about 40 words)

key_points: Benefit: Can maintain soil fertility and provide higher returns.
Drawback: Over-intensification with exhaustive crops rapidly depletes nutrients.

sub_questions.solution: A major benefit of proper crop rotation is its ability to simultaneously yield higher agricultural returns and naturally maintain soil fertility. Conversely, a severe drawback occurs when farmers aggressively rotate consecutive soil-exhaustive crops, which drastically accelerates the depletion of soil nutrients.

sub_questions.text_english: Which of the following is the main takeaway from the study mentioned in the passage?

options_english.A: The study needs to include more valid data to support the practice of crop rotation.
options_english.B: Crop rotation is a sustainable practice that can transform the agricultural sector.
options_english.C: The impact of crop rotation on farmer's upliftment has been thoroughly explained.
options_english.D: Crop rotation is independent of the type of crops harvested and availability of water for irrigation.

sub_questions.solution: Option B is correct. The fundamental takeaway from the text and the presented study is that crop rotation, when properly managed rather than intensely exploited, is a crucial sustainable practice fundamentally designed to transform and maintain agricultural productivity.

sub_questions.text_english:
Read the given sentence from a science journal. Identify the error and supply the correction in the sentence.
'When nutrition therapy is provided by a qualified professional, people could learn how to make better food choices.'
sub_questions.solution: The sentence states a general fact or a present possibility ('is provided'), so the present modal of ability 'can' must be used instead of the past/conditional modal 'could'. The corrected sentence is: 'When nutrition therapy is provided by a qualified professional, people can learn how to make better food choices.'

sub_questions.text_english:
Fill in the blank by using the correct form of the word in the brackets, for the given portion of a letter.
Please keep me _______ (apprise) of your next step to address this matter. Thanks for your time.
sub_questions.solution: The correct grammatical form required here is the past participle used as a passive adjective. The corrected phrase is: 'Please keep me apprised of your next step...'

sub_questions.text_english:
Sunanda and Pushkar had a conversation about their travels. Report Pushkar's question.
Have you ever been to Peri Bagh ?

key_points: Pushkar asked Sunanda if/whether she had ever been to Peri Bagh.

sub_questions.solution: When reporting a direct yes/no question, the conjunction 'if' or 'whether' is used, and the present perfect tense ('Have you ever been') shifts back to the past perfect tense ('had ever been'). The reported speech is: Pushkar asked Sunanda if she had ever been to Peri Bagh.

sub_questions.text_english:
Read the dialogue between Vilakshna and her physician, Dr. Sharnani, regarding the effectiveness of her medication.
Dr. Sharnani: How is your acid reflux problem now?
Vilakshna: I'd tried everything without success, but this new medicine is great.
Select the correct option to complete the reporting of the above dialogue.
Dr. Sharnani asked Vilakshna about her acid reflux problem to which Vilakshna replied that she'd tried everything without success, _______

options_english.A: but she found the new medicine to be great
options_english.B: but she thought that this new medicine was great
options_english.C: but the new medicine was great
options_english.D: but that new medicine was great

sub_questions.solution: Option D is correct. In reported speech, the present tense verb 'is' strictly changes to the past tense 'was', and the demonstrative pronoun 'this' changes to 'that'. Therefore, 'but this new medicine is great' becomes 'but that new medicine was great'.

sub_questions.text_english:
Identify the error and supply the correction for the given sentence from a private coaching institute's advertisement.
Are you living a happy life? Do you want to find your identification? Do you want to enhance your career?
sub_questions.solution: The word 'identification' typically refers to a physical document or the act of identifying something. In the context of philosophical self-discovery and personal career growth, the correct conceptual noun is 'identity'. The corrected sentence is: 'Do you want to find your identity?'

sub_questions.text_english:
Fill in the blank by choosing the correct option to complete the line from an insurance company brochure.
Suitable for someone who wishes to _______ (insure/assure/ensure) adequate financial backup. It is available to the family in case of his/her untimely death.
sub_questions.solution: The verb 'ensure' precisely means to make absolutely certain that something will occur or be available. In this context, the person wishes to make certain there is an adequate financial backup, making 'ensure' the correct choice over 'insure' (provide policy) or 'assure' (give confidence).

sub_questions.text_english:
Select the option that identifies the error and supplies the correction for a pop-up that appeared on a webpage.
These cookies are used to collect information about how you interact with our website and allows us to remember you.
sub_questions.solution: Option D is correct. The compound subject 'These cookies' is unequivocally plural. Therefore, the verbs connected by 'and' must both be plural. The singular verb 'allows' must be corrected to the plural verb 'allow' to maintain strict subject-verb agreement.

sub_questions.text_english:
Complete the given narrative by filling in the blank with the correct option.
I _______ watching that programme every week since it started.
sub_questions.solution: Option C is correct. The presence of the phrase 'since it started' clearly indicates an ongoing action that began in the past and is still continuing in the present. This requires the present perfect continuous tense 'have been watching', which aligns perfectly with the first-person pronoun 'I'.

sub_questions.text_english:
Report the following dialogue between two friends who are visiting a museum, by completing the sentence.
Auronima : What are you staring at ?
Soumitra: I am in awe of this beautiful painting! I have not seen anything like this before.
Auronima asked Soumitra what he was staring at. Soumitra exclaimed that he was in awe of the beautiful painting and that _______

fill_values: he had not seen anything like that before

sub_questions.solution: When converting direct speech to reported speech, the present perfect tense 'have not seen' must backshift to the past perfect tense 'had not seen'. Additionally, the demonstrative pronoun 'this' changes to 'that'. The correctly completed sentence is: '...and that he had not seen anything like that before.'

sub_questions.text_english:
Fill in the blank by choosing the correct option to complete the weather warning given by the IMD.
IMD on Sunday _______ a 'thunderstorm' alert for some districts in coastal Maharashtra in view of the extremely severe cyclonic storm Biparjoy gushing over the Arabian Sea.
sub_questions.solution: Option C is correct. The time phrase 'on Sunday' in the context of reporting a completed alert indicates a finished past action. Therefore, the simple past tense 'issued' is grammatically accurate to describe an action that has already concluded.

sub_questions.text_english:
Complete the slogan, by filling in the blank with the correct option.
When it gets really hot, rain _______ a blessing.
sub_questions.solution: Option B is correct. Slogans often state definitive outcomes or guaranteed results based on a condition. The modal 'will be' perfectly expresses the absolute certainty and natural consequence that rain becomes a blessing during extreme heat.

sub_questions.text_english:
Identify the error and supply the correction for the following advertisement of an antivirus software.
A properly installed and maintained antivirus program may wipe out any malware attack, be it a bot, a virus, a Trojan or even ransomware.
sub_questions.solution: In an advertisement highlighting the specific capability and definitive strength of a software product, the modal of ability or certainty should be used. The modal 'may' implies weak possibility, which contradicts the marketing tone. It must be replaced with 'can' or 'will'. The corrected phrase is: '...antivirus program can wipe out...'

sub_questions.text_english: (a) The problem of speeding traffic on colony roads causing accidents is increasing day by day. As a young citizen, who wants to minimize the accidents caused by them, write a letter to the editor of a national daily, in about 120 words, expressing your concern at the situation and suggesting measures to resolve the problem and drawing attention of the concerned authorities. You are Samyukta Khanna/Sanjay Khanna of 567, Madhur Apartments, Amar Vihar, Aram Nagar.

key_points: Format: Sender address, Date, Receiver address, Subject, Salutation, Closing.
Express deep concern over the alarming rise in speeding traffic on residential roads.
Highlight the direct threat posed to vulnerable pedestrians like children and the elderly.
Suggest concrete measures: install speed breakers, strict penalties, and deployment of traffic police.
Polite appeal to authorities for prompt and strict enforcement.

sub_questions.solution:
567, Madhur Apartments,
Amar Vihar, Aram Nagar.

15th May 2024

The Editor,
The National Daily,
New Delhi.

Subject: Deep concern over speeding traffic and increasing accidents on colony roads.

Sir/Madam,
Through the columns of your esteemed newspaper, I wish to draw the urgent attention of the concerned authorities towards the alarming increase in speeding traffic and subsequent fatal accidents on our local residential roads. 

Reckless driving by everyday commuters has effectively transformed our quiet streets into dangerous hazard zones. This daily menace poses a severe and continuous threat to vulnerable pedestrians, especially young children playing outdoors and the elderly out for walks. Despite our repeated complaints to the local council, no concrete preventive action has been taken.

I strongly suggest the immediate installation of prominent speed breakers at crucial intersections. Furthermore, deploying traffic personnel during peak hours to actively monitor speeds and heavily penalize violators is imperative. Strict enforcement of residential speed limits is necessary to ensure our collective safety.

I hope the authorities will take prompt action to avert any further tragic accidents in our neighbourhood.

Yours sincerely,
Samyukta Khanna

sub_questions.text_english: (b) As Kaveri Mahajan, of 543, Narmada Apartments, Jeev Nagar, you feel that during the monsoon season all the rain water goes down the drain without being utilized. Write a letter to the RWA of your society, in about 120 words, suggesting measures to save and preserve rain water emphasizing the importance of saving every drop of water.

key_points: Format: Sender address, Date, Receiver address, Subject, Salutation, Closing.
Highlight the sheer wastage of rainwater flowing into drains during the current monsoon.
Emphasize the critical importance of water conservation given future scarcities.
Propose practical measures: install a society-wide rainwater harvesting system.
Suggest utilizing collected water for common needs like gardening and washing.

sub_questions.solution:
543, Narmada Apartments,
Jeev Nagar.

20th July 2024

The President,
Resident Welfare Association,
Jeev Nagar.

Subject: Urgent proposal to implement rainwater harvesting in our society.

Dear Sir/Madam,
I am writing to highlight a highly crucial issue regarding water conservation within our residential complex. During the ongoing heavy monsoon season, it is deeply disheartening to witness thousands of gallons of precious rainwater blindly flowing down the municipal drains without being utilized.

Given the constantly looming threat of urban water scarcity, it is imperative that we as a community understand the monumental value of saving every single drop. I strongly propose that our RWA immediately install a comprehensive rainwater harvesting system within the society premises. The systematically collected water can be efficiently utilized for maintaining our common parks, washing the parking areas, and significantly recharging the local depleted groundwater table.

I urge the committee to consider and implement these sustainable measures promptly to secure a better future for our society.

Yours sincerely,
Kaveri Mahajan

sub_questions.text_english:
(a) Co-curricular activities help to enhance holistic development and assist in inculcating critical skills and abilities to be successful and happy in the 21st century life and workplace. Based on the table given below, write an analytical paragraph, in about 120 words, on how co-curricular activities supplement the theoretical curriculum.

ESSENTIAL SKILLS AND VALUES THAT CAN BE DEVELOPED THROUGH CO-CURRICULAR ACTIVITIES
- logical and analytical thinking
- creative and critical thinking
- problem-solving skills
- leadership skills
- social, emotional and communication skills
- recreational value
- enhanced technology skills

key_points: Introduce the concept that co-curricular activities actively supplement dry theoretical learning.
Detail how they build cognitive skills like logical, creative, and critical thinking.
Mention interpersonal growth through leadership and communication skills development.
Highlight the crucial recreational value and stress relief they provide to students.
Conclude that these activities are absolutely essential for holistic 21st-century success.

sub_questions.solution: Co-curricular activities are no longer mere optional pastimes; they have become essential, dynamic components that robustly supplement the traditional theoretical curriculum by fostering true holistic development. While standard classroom learning primarily imparts academic knowledge, structured activities like debates, organized sports, and specialized clubs actively cultivate crucial 21st-century survival skills. They tangibly develop logical, analytical, and highly critical thinking abilities, empowering students to tackle real-world problems creatively and efficiently. Furthermore, consistent teamwork inherently builds strong leadership, deep social empathy, and vital emotional communication skills, perfectly preparing individuals for complex future workplace dynamics. Beyond strict skill acquisition, these activities offer immense and necessary recreational value, significantly alleviating academic stress while simultaneously enhancing modern technology skills. Ultimately, these co-curriculars perfectly bridge the gap between textbook theories and practical life success.

sub_questions.text_english:
(b) Tourism stands as a cornerstone of the nation's development. The following table provides an insight into the multifaceted impact and positive contributions of tourism. Write an analytical paragraph in about 120 words assessing the significance of tourism.

IMPACT OF TOURISM
- contributes to GDP and foreign exchange
- boosts local markets and businesses
- creates employment
- preserves culture
- promotes infrastructural development

key_points: Introduce tourism as a fundamental cornerstone and driver of national development.
Discuss its massive economic contribution to the GDP and valuable foreign exchange.
Explain how it actively boosts local markets, creates widespread employment, and uplifts communities.
Highlight its role in carefully preserving indigenous culture and promoting heritage.
Conclude with its positive catalyst effect on robust infrastructural development.

sub_questions.solution: Tourism has undeniably emerged as a highly vital cornerstone for our nation's holistic development, showcasing a deeply multifaceted and overwhelmingly positive impact. Economically, the sector serves as a massive driver of national growth, significantly contributing to the overarching GDP while simultaneously generating highly valuable foreign exchange reserves. This massive influx of capital directly revitalizes and boosts local markets, breathing necessary economic life into small, regional businesses. Furthermore, tourism acts as a prolific creator of diverse employment opportunities, ranging from broad hospitality to niche local artisanship, thereby drastically reducing regional unemployment rates. Beyond mere economics, tourism plays a pivotal and sensitive role in preserving and globally proudly promoting our rich indigenous culture. Finally, the absolute necessity to comfortably accommodate tourists serves as a permanent catalyst for robust, long-term infrastructural development.

questions.text_english:
(a) For the first twenty-four hours, Mijbil was neither hostile nor friendly; he was simply aloof and indifferent, choosing to sleep on the floor as far from my bed as possible. The second night Mijbil came on to my bed in the small hours and remained asleep in the crook of my knees until the servant brought tea in the morning, and during the day he began to lose his apathy and take a keen, much too keen, interest in his surroundings. I made a body-belt for him and took him on a lead to the bathroom, where for half an hour he went wild with joy in the water.
(Mijbil the Otter)
questions.instruction_line_english: Read the following extract and answer the questions:

sub_questions.text_english: Which of the following is not a reason why Mijbil came on to Maxwell's bed in the small hours ?

options_english.A: He had started taking interest in his surroundings.
options_english.B: He was becoming friendly with Maxwell.
options_english.C: He wanted to play with Maxwell on his bed.
options_english.D: He wanted to feel safe and not remain indifferent.

sub_questions.solution: Option C is correct. The extract details Mijbil coming to the bed to sleep securely in the crook of Maxwell's knees, gradually losing apathy, and beginning to take an interest in his surroundings. However, there is absolutely no textual evidence suggesting his motive was to actively 'play with Maxwell on his bed' at that specific early hour.

sub_questions.text_english: Maxwell says that Mijbil was neither hostile nor friendly, he was simply aloof and indifferent for the first twenty-four hours. Give reasons in not more than 40 words.

key_points: Mijbil was in a completely unfamiliar and new environment.
He needed adequate time and space to adapt, overcome fear, and establish trust.

sub_questions.solution: Mijbil's initial aloof and indifferent behaviour was entirely natural because he had been suddenly thrust into a completely new, strange, and unfamiliar environment. Being abruptly separated from his wild habitat, he desperately needed quiet time and space to cautiously adapt, feel safe, and trust his new human owner.

sub_questions.text_english: Read the following descriptions (A) - (D) and identify which one correctly corresponds to the extract.

options_english.A: Owning a pet is tedious and needs commitment.
options_english.B: A pet needs his own space and time to get adjusted to his owner's environment.
options_english.C: Maxwell decided to bring Mijbil because he was very sad to lose his dog.

sub_questions.solution: Option B is correct. The extract perfectly illustrates the gradual progression of a wild animal's behaviour, demonstrating that a new pet intrinsically requires its own undisturbed space, time, and extreme patience from the owner to comfortably adjust to a completely new environment before becoming friendly.

sub_questions.text_english: Which characteristic trait of otters is revealed when Mijbil is taken to the bathroom?

key_points: Otters possess an immense, wild love and profound natural affinity for water.

sub_questions.solution: The distinct characteristic trait revealed is that otters possess an incredibly intense, almost wild love and natural affinity for water; they enthusiastically go 'wild with joy' when allowed to freely play and splash in it.

questions.solution: Extract-based question set. Answers are provided in sub_questions.

questions.text_english:
(b) The arrival of a stranger at an inn in winter was in any case an unusual event. A stranger of such uncommon appearance set all tongues wagging. Mrs. Hall, the landlord's wife, made every effort to be friendly. But Griffin had no desire to talk, and told her, My reason for coming to Iping is a desire for solitude. I do not wish to be disturbed in my work. Besides, an accident has affected my face.
Satisfied that her guest was an eccentric scientist, and in view of the fact that he had paid her in advance, Mrs. Hall was prepared to excuse his strange habits and irritable temper.
(Footprints Without Feet)
questions.instruction_line_english: Read the following extract and answer the questions:

sub_questions.text_english:
State any one inference about Griffin from the given context
My reason for coming to Iping is a desire for solitude. I do not wish to be disturbed in my work. Besides, an accident has affected my face.

key_points: Griffin is highly secretive, antisocial, and protective of his privacy.

sub_questions.solution: A direct inference is that Griffin is deeply secretive, deliberately antisocial, and highly protective of his absolute privacy, actively manufacturing excuses to avoid any normal social interaction or scrutiny from the village locals.

sub_questions.text_english:
State True or False:
Even though Mrs. Hall was satisfied with Griffin, she was skeptical to excuse his strange habits and irritable temper.
sub_questions.solution: The statement is explicitly false. The final line of the extract clearly states that because he had paid her in advance and she believed he was an eccentric scientist, 'Mrs. Hall was prepared to excuse his strange habits and irritable temper', showing no skepticism in accepting the money.

sub_questions.text_english: It was not difficult for Griffin to convince the landlord and his wife about his strange appearance and eccentric behaviour. Elaborate in about 40 words with reference to the context.

sub_questions.text_english:
(a) Grief or sadness is an emotion natural to all types of loss or significant change. You have been asked to present an analysis of the approaches of Lencho and Kisa Gotami in dealing with their respective losses. Write this presentation draft including your insights, and comparing the approaches of both.
You may begin like this: One acknowledges that Lencho had unwavering faith in God whereas Kisa Gotami in her grief, believed that her son ....... however .......
(Reference - A Letter to God and The Sermon at Benares)

key_points: Contrast Lencho's material loss with Gotami's irreplaceable human loss.
Lencho responded with highly proactive but blind faith, writing directly to God.
Gotami initially responded with absolute frantic denial, seeking impossible medicine.
Gotami eventually achieved profound spiritual enlightenment regarding universal death.
Lencho remained utterly ignorant of human kindness, showing no spiritual growth.

sub_questions.solution: One acknowledges that Lencho had unwavering faith in God whereas Kisa Gotami in her profound grief, initially believed her son could miraculously be brought back to life. However, their ultimate approaches to devastating loss sharply contrast. When Lencho's entire livelihood was utterly destroyed by a hailstorm, he did not mourn hopelessly but immediately took proactive action, fiercely demanding money directly from God. His approach was intensely practical yet entirely grounded in blind, innocent faith, leading him to cynically suspect humanity. Conversely, Kisa Gotami was completely consumed by frantic denial over her child's death, desperately seeking medicine. It was only through Lord Buddha's profound guidance that she actively realized the unavoidable, universal nature of death. While Lencho's material loss merely fueled his stubborn faith, Gotami's irreplaceable loss ultimately led her to profound spiritual awakening.

sub_questions.text_english:
(b) You have been chosen to address the school assembly on the occasion of Women's Day. You choose to speak on the resilience and indomitable spirit of the young girls: Anne Frank and Valli. Prepare the speech draft, with reference to the commonality and contrast in the situations and circumstances of both the girls.
(Madam Rides the Bus and From the Diary of Anne Frank)
You may begin like this: Good morning everyone. Today, I'd like to express my insights on the resilience of two young girls .......
You may end this way: To conclude I'd like to say that ....... Thank you.

key_points: Format: Speech opening and closing.
Highlight Anne Frank's mental resilience and hope amidst severe Holocaust oppression.
Highlight Valli's fierce independence, meticulous planning, and courage to travel alone.
Contrast their situations: Anne fighting for basic emotional survival, Valli aggressively chasing a dream.
Conclude that true courage and mature resilience are completely independent of age.

sub_questions.solution: Good morning everyone. Today, I'd like to express my profound insights on the immense resilience of two remarkably courageous young girls, Anne Frank and Valli. Both extraordinary girls exhibited an indomitable spirit, though their historical circumstances were vastly different. Anne, tragically trapped in a highly confined annex during the horrifying Holocaust, brilliantly used her diary to preserve her sanity, powerful voice, and sharp intellect amidst unimaginable daily fear. Her resilience lay in her pure mental fortitude and enduring hope. On the other hand, eight-year-old Valli lived a peaceful rural life but harboured a deep, fierce desire to independently ride the bus. Her resilience was flawlessly showcased through her extremely meticulous planning, immense self-control in saving pennies, and her bold journey into the massive outside world. To conclude I'd like to say that their powerful stories prove true courage is entirely independent of age. Thank you.

(a) Imagine that Hari Singh from 'The Thief's Story' by Ruskin Bond, writes a diary entry, exploring the theme of human values and relations that are essential in life and can transform a person in the context of his own experience. Write this diary entry as Hari Singh.
(The Thief's Story)

key_points: Format: Diary entry (Date, Salutation).
Express intense inner conflict at the train station regarding the stolen money.
Reflect deeply on Anil's unconditional trust, kindness, and promise of education.
Realize that genuine human values and respect are far more permanently valuable than temporary stolen wealth.
Conclude with the powerful, transformative decision to return the money and change.

sub_questions.solution:
Dear Diary,
Tonight, my guilty heart is incredibly heavy yet strangely filled with a profound, warm peace. I had the absolute perfect opportunity to successfully run away with Anil's stolen money. I was standing at the dark station, the speeding train was right there, but an invisible force firmly held me back. It was solely the vivid memory of Anil's incredibly kind face and his absolute, unconditional trust in me. He generously took me in when I was a struggling nobody, fed me, and most importantly, he actively began teaching me how to read and write. I suddenly realized that a few stolen hundreds would only last a week, but proper education could permanently make me a truly big, highly respected man. Genuine human values like pure trust and affection are immensely more powerful than any wealth. I have returned the money because I desperately want to be entirely worthy of him. Hari.

sub_questions.text_english: (b) A character arc is the transformation or development of a character throughout a story and refers to the changes a character undergoes as a result of his/her experiences, challenges and interactions with other characters. In the light of the above information, trace the character arc of Bholi in K.A. Abbas's 'Bholi'.

key_points: Initial state: Bholi was an immensely frightened, severely neglected, and stammering girl.
Turning point: Her compassionate teacher provided profound affection and crucial educational empowerment.
Gradual change: Education instilled deep self-confidence, completely altering her inner psyche.
Climax: She fiercely rejected the greedy Bishamber, throwing away the marriage garland.
Final state: Transformed into 'Sulekha', an empowered, highly independent, and self-respecting woman.

sub_questions.solution: Bholi’s magnificent character arc represents a highly beautiful and immensely inspiring journey from a deeply marginalized, incredibly timid girl to a fierce, highly independent young woman. Initially, strictly due to unfortunate physical flaws and a severe speech stammer, Bholi was entirely neglected by her cruel family and subjected to constant, humiliating mockery. She was treated merely as a frightened, silent 'dumb cow'. The monumental pivotal turning point in her tragic life was her interaction with her highly compassionate school teacher, who actively provided her with immense affection, instilled deep self-confidence, and completely empowered her through structured education. The spectacular climax of her arc dramatically occurs during her forced wedding to the disgustingly greedy Bishamber. When he cruelly demands a dowry, the once-timid Bholi courageously throws away the garland, firmly refusing the match. She confidently declares her noble intention to independently teach, completing her glorious transformation into Sulekha.
